designs.competitor_comparison:
Matching HW-ring's effective INT8 throughput on a 4x4 grid at L = 4096 (1,498 MAC/cycle) with dedicated BOS INT8 arrays would take 23.4 arrays x 15,797 = 369,750 um2, which is +70.8% of the grid. The bit-plane mode adds 7,885 um2 (+1.51%). SC efficiency of the whole chip would fall to 459 GMAC/s/mm2 with BOS, against 773 with bit-plane.

Equal-throughput BOS area for the other precisions (W4A8 uses BOS INT6 as a proxy):
- W4A8: 534,794 um2 (102.5% of the grid).
- INT4: 886,148 um2 (169.8%).

A small add-on, for example one BOS array (3.0% of a 4x4 grid), gives only 64 MAC/cycle. That is about 23x less INT8 throughput than HW-ring for twice its area.

Where BOS is better:
- As a standalone INT engine it is denser (1,620 GMAC/s/mm2 against HW-ring's 1,131 at L = 4096).
- It needs only about 0.5-2 bits/MAC of operand bandwidth against 4 at the 4x4 edge.
- It is not drain-limited at short K.

So BOS wins only if INT dominates the workload or the memory system cannot supply the bit-plane bandwidth. Against the other INT-mode angle, Booth all-space, see the angle field: Booth is better for K <= ~1024 or when bandwidth is limited.
designs.verdict_on_user_shift_down_idea:
Shifting the tile accumulator down (LSB first) every cycle does not work here, for three reasons:
1. A low bit can only be shifted out once every contribution of that weight has arrived. That happens after the whole reduction for that plane pair, not every cycle, and PaYN's accumulator persists across many cycles and blocks.
2. In bit-plane order the weight 2^(i+j) jumps by more than one step between cycles, so a fixed 1-bit shift does not match.
3. The accumulator is segmented (9-bit acc_low + pending carry/borrow + lazy +-1 acc_high). A per-cycle shift would need the pending flags flushed, a 24-bit shift mux in every tile (~9-19 um2/tile, i.e. 1.8-3.7% of a 4x4 grid paid in SC mode too), and storage for the emitted bits.

The intuition does work when it is moved to where shifting is cheap:
- (a) Put the weight classes in space (rows = activation bits). The existing drain then shifts the per-plane partial sums out every cycle into one shift-add (Horner) combiner at the east edge, one per PE row, amortized over 64*P_C tiles. This is literally "shift the results" at zero tile cost.
- (b) For weight bits in time, shift the results only between whole-reduction passes, MSB first (Horner left shift): rotate them once around the PE's own drain chain with a <<1 at the PE boundary. That is 8 cycles per pass and about 163 um2 per PE.
- An LSB-first "shift down" at the edge would be equivalent but has to collect the emitted bits, so MSB-first Horner is the cheaper form.
risks: Operand bandwidth is the decisive system cost. INT mode needs 1024 fresh bits/cycle per edge half: 8192 bits/cycle = 409.6 GB/s per 4x4 grid, which is 14x SC's average binary traffic and 2.7x Booth all-space per MAC. Weights must be stored bit-plane-major, and activations need a K-byte replay buffer per PE row or 8x re-reads. The SRAM banking area is not in the composite. If the system cannot supply this, Booth all-space is the better INT mode.

Drain and skew overhead at grid scale: effective INT8 is only 0.81 MAC/cycle/tile at K=1024 on 4x4 and 0.66 on 4x8. At K <= ~1024, Booth all-space with a ring is equal or better. The gain needs K >= ~2048 (1.46 at K=4096). On a single PE the ring gains nothing over BP-S.
All areas are cell-count estimates, not synthesis. The combiner tree size and the buffering of the 192 return wires per PE (allowed for at 28 um2, up to 56) are the softest numbers.
Timing of the ring return path (canonical 15-bit acc_high ripple + ~171 um wire + 2 AO22) is estimated at ~1.2 ns of 2.5 ns, but it is untimed, and no PaYN grid has been routed.
The output footprint per PE drops from 8x8 (SC) to 1x8 (INT8/W4A8) or 2x8 (INT4). Filling the grid needs M >= P_R and N >= 8*P_C, and GEMV uses 1/P_R of the grid.

The HB schedule for W4A8/INT4 keeps the whole output in the 24-bit tile (W4A8 safe for K <= 8,191 worst case) and needs bit-plane-major activations, i.e. a runtime corner-turn in the data mover. INT8 HB is not allowed.

Entering INT mode requires binary_q = 0 (reset, or a zero load with int_mode = 0); otherwise comparator bits corrupt the raw bits. Outputs above 24 bits (up to ~2^14*K) must be accepted by the writeback/requant path.
Power was not measured. In INT mode all 2048 bit-pipe bits and the popcounts toggle with random data. In SC mode the 1024 edge ORs per half add an estimated ~2% on a single PE and ~0.5% at 4x4.

designs.name: WO-ring: weight-outer Booth-digit Horner with a zero-tile per-PE drain ring
designs.angle: Smallest possible tile change with weight-outer order. Each pass streams the whole reduction for one digit weight, and the stationary segmented accumulator gets a Horner shift between passes. Compared: MSB-first shift up against LSB-first shift down with emitted bits, a shift in the same cycle as a MAC against a dedicated shift slot, an in-tile shifter against an edge or drain-ring shifter. Applied to the lane-product (Booth digit) family and the bit-plane family.
designs.plain_summary: Yes, and the tile does not change. Split a into radix-4 digits d_a (-2..2) and w into radix-16 digits d_w (-8..8). Each cycle, lane k carries one digit pair. a_bits[k][m] is set on 0, 8 or 16 positions and w_bits[k][m] on 2|d_w| positions, placed so that count[k] = sum_m bits[k][m] = |d_a|*|d_w|. sign[k] = a_sign[k] ^ w_sign[k] gives the sign. The existing comparators produce these bits when the Sobol bus is forced to a fixed preset. Stream the whole reduction once per digit, most significant first. Between passes, multiply every accumulator by 4 by circulating it once around its PE row through the drain chain and one new 24-bit mux per row (8 idle cycles). Shifting down also works, but the dropped bits must be stored. Cost: 0.47% of a 4x4 grid. INT8 runs at 0.87-0.97 MAC/cycle/tile, W4A8 at 1.6-1.9, INT4 at 2.9-3.8.
designs.mapping:
**Digits.** Each lane carries one Booth digit pair per cycle.
- a (two's complement INT8/INT4) becomes radix-4 Booth digits d_a[p] in [-2,2]: p=0..3 for INT8, 0..1 for INT4.
- w becomes radix-16 Booth digits d_w[q] in [-8,8]: q=0..1 for INT8. An INT4 w is its own single digit.
- a*w = sum_{p,q} 2^(2p+4q) d_a[p] d_w[q].

**Per cycle.** In pass p, cycle t, lane k carries reduction index kk = kbase + 8t + k.
- a_binary_in[h][k] = CODE_A[k][|d_a[p](A[i][kk])|] and a_signs_in[h][k] = (d_a < 0).
- w_binary_in[v][k] = CODE_W[k][|d_w[q](W[kk][j])|] and w_signs_in[v][k] = (d_w < 0).
- Padding and zero digits use code 0 and sign 0.
- Both Sobol random-value buses are forced to PRESET_A / PRESET_W (16 bytes each, listed in the model).

**Comparators (unchanged).** Each bit is bit = code > PRESET[m] ^ MASK(k,m).
- a_bits[k][m] is {} / R0_k / all 16 positions for |d_a| = 0 / 1 / 2. R0_k is the 8 lowest thresholds of lane k.
- w_bits[k][m] covers the first |d_w| pairs of lane k's W threshold ranking. Every pair holds exactly one R0_k position.
- So count[k] = |d_a|*|d_w| <= 16 = M, and sign[k] = a_sign ^ w_sign. This is verified exhaustively for all 8 k on both banks.
- Code tables come from the data mover, e.g. k=0: CODE_A = [0,73,245], CODE_W = [0,35,53,61,115,144,150,195,240].

**Tiles.**
- Tile row h = activation i = 8r + h.
- FH: tile column v = weight j = 8c + v, with both digits in time (8x8 outputs per PE).
- HYS (INT8, chunk >= 512): column v = weight j = 4c + (v>>1), carrying W digit q = v&1 (8x4 outputs per PE).
- W4A8 and INT4: j = 8c + v.
- The 8 lanes are 8 consecutive k. All 128 AND positions are used.
designs.schedule:
**Common terms.** Order is weight-outer: the whole reduction chunk (length L) streams once per digit pass, most significant digit first.
- C = ceil(L/8) cycles per pass.
- A rotation (ring) is 8 slots.
- A drain plus skew flush is D = 8*P_C + P_R + P_C - 2 slots: 8 for 1 PE, 38 for 4x4, 74 for 4x8.

**INT8 HYS** (used for L >= 512, chunk <= 8191), per 8x4-output PE block:
1. Pass p=3: X = sum_k d_a3*d_wq.
2. Ring: X = 4X.
3. Pass p=2: X = sum_k (4 d_a3 + d_a2) d_wq.
4. Ring, then pass p=1.
5. Ring, then pass p=0: X = sum_k a_k*d_wq(w_kj).
6. Drain. The collector forms out_ij = (X_{j,1} << 4) + X_{j,0}. The two values leave on consecutive drain edges.
- Cycles = 4C + 24 + D per 8x4 block, i.e. 8C + 48 + 2D per 8x8 outputs.

**INT8 FH** (used for L <= 511), per 8x8 block:
- Passes in weight order: (3,1)=10, (2,1)=8, (3,0)+(1,1)=6, (2,0)+(0,1)=4, (1,0)=2, (0,0)=0.
- One ring after each weight group (5 rings), then one drain.
- After the last pass, X = sum_k a_k*w_k.
- Cycles = 8C + 40 + D.

**W4A8:** p = 3..0, 3 rings, 1 drain: 4C + 24 + D per 8x8 block (chunk 8191).

**INT4:** p = 1, 0, 1 ring: 2C + 8 + D (chunk 131071).

**Effective MAC/cycle/tile** (slot counts checked against the model):

| mode | grid | K=511 | K=1024 | K=4096 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| INT8 | 1 PE | 0.912 | 0.941 | 0.985 |
| INT8 | 4x4 | 0.866 | 0.892 | 0.971 |
| INT8 | 4x8 | 0.816 | 0.839 | 0.954 |
| W4A8 | 4x4 | 1.607 | 1.784 | 1.941 |
| INT4 | 4x4 | 2.937 | 3.391 | 3.828 |

The FH/HYS crossover is K = 512 in all three grids.
designs.shift_mechanism:
**Mechanism.** A drain ring per PE row with a hard-wired x4 shift and no tile change. PE RTL:
- acc_chain[0][h] = ring_q ? {acc_chain[N_W][h][21:0], 2'b00} : acc_in_west[h]
- tile shift_in = shift_in | ring_q
- ring_q <= ring_in (sync reset 0), re-exported east with the A pipes.

**Each of the 8 consecutive ring edges.** Every tile does exactly what a drain does:
- acc_low <= acc_in[8:0], acc_high <= acc_in[23:9], pending_carry/borrow <= 0.
- acc_in is the west tile's canonical acc_out = {acc_high + pend_c - pend_b, acc_low}.
- Tile 0 takes 4x the east tile's canonical value.

**Why it is exact.**
- A pending carry or borrow left by the last MAC is folded into the moving value at the first ring edge, so it is never lost.
- After 8 edges every value has passed the x4 wiring once and is back in its own tile, 4x larger mod 2^24. That is exact within the chunk limits.
- No accumulate shares a cycle with a shift: shift_in has priority and the feed sends 8 idle slots. So the LOW_W=9 single carry/borrow invariant is untouched; the model saw low_sum in [-128, 632].

**Grid timing.** ring_q is one flop per PE.
- The controller drives PE(r,0) one cycle after the slot's load, skewed by r.
- ring_q hops east exactly like a_bits_pipe, so each PE rotates on its own skewed idle slots. There is no grid-skew bubble per rotation.

**LSB-first variant (the user's idea).** The same mux input is wired as {2{e[23]}, e[23:2]}, and e[1:0] goes to an emitted-bit buffer.

**Rejected alternatives.**
- acc <- 4acc + d in one cycle: low_sum reaches 2172, so 0..4 carries are needed. That requires SUM_W+2, multi-unit pending and a 15-bit shift mux on acc_high, about 20 um2/tile.
- In-tile 1-cycle x4 (a 3rd input on the 24 AO22 drain muxes): 9.9 um2/tile = 1.96% of 4x4, for only +4-6% INT throughput.
- One global ring per grid row: 0.13% of area, but each rotation costs 38 slots (4x4) or 74 (4x8).
designs.sign_handling:
- **Signs:** the per-lane sign is the digit sign, carried on the existing sign path: a_signs_in = (d_a < 0) and w_signs_in = (d_w < 0).
- **Per-cycle load:** signs reload every cycle with load_a/load_w and load_*_sign held high. The PE sign pipes already take a per-cycle enable.
- **Tile arithmetic:** the existing 5 XORs per lane plus the -16*N correction row turn count[k] into +-|d_a||d_w| exactly. A zero digit gives 0 for either sign.
- **Two's complement:** -128 and -8 need no negative pass or MSB-plane handling, because the Booth MSB digit already carries the negative weight.
- **Power side effect:** the -16N row now changes every cycle (power only).
- **Sign-magnitude data** (magnitude <= 127) is recoded to two's complement and then Booth digits by the data mover.

bandwidth.notes:
**Per-PE feed.** Each lane needs one fresh 8-bit code plus a sign every cycle: (64 A + 64 W lanes) x 9 = 1,152 b/cycle/PE. That exactly fills the existing a/w_binary_in (512) + signs (64) per side, every cycle. SC uses those ports 1 cycle in 8 (144 b/cycle average).

**Bits per MAC at peak:**

| | 1 PE | 4x4 | 4x8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| INT8 | 18 | 4.5 | 3.375 |
| W4A8 | 9 | 2.25 | 1.69 |
| INT4 | 4.5 | 1.125 | 0.84 |
| SC | 2.25 | 0.56 | 0.42 |

4x4 feeds 4,608 b/cycle (8 sides x 576) for 1,024 MAC/cycle; 4x8 feeds 6,912 b/cycle.

**Re-read factor.** One delivery per digit pass: 8 for INT8 (HYS: 4 A passes; W 4 passes x 2 digit columns), 4 for W4A8, 2 for INT4.

**Do the ports suffice?** Yes for the Booth lane family, but SRAM must sustain 8x SC's average edge rate. A compact-digit feed (3 + 5 bits per lane) with a small edge decoder (~3.7k um2 in 4x4) would cut it to 2,048 b/cycle in 4x4. The bit-plane family needs 1,024 b/side/cycle (2x the ports) plus a comparator bypass.

designs.sc_mode_impact:
**Area.** No tile change.
- +147.9 um2 per PE (0.51% of u_pe) plus 101.1 um2 Sobol preset per grid.
- That is +0.566% (1 PE), +0.473% (4x4) and +0.476% (4x8) of array area.
- SC area efficiency: 581.6 -> 578.3, 784.8 -> 781.1, 806.3 -> 802.4 GMAC/s/mm2.
- The east collector (+2,546 um2 in 4x4/4x8) belongs to the memory system. Counting it gives 0.96% (4x4) and 0.73% (4x8).

**Timing.**
- Tile critical path unchanged.
- The ring mux sits only on tile column 0's acc_in, which is the drain path, not the MAC path. Its ~170 um east-to-west return is estimated at about 1 ns of the 2.5 ns period.
- The preset gate is in the Sobol D path, off the worst reg-to-reg path (Sobol -> comparator -> w_bits_pipe, +0.307 ns).
- The OR of ring_q into shift_in adds about 30 ps to today's WNS path (+0.146 ns). Retiming shift_in by one flop is the fallback.

**Power.** In SC, ring_q=0 and int_mode=0 are static. The only cost is leakage of ~2.5k um2 per 4x4 (0.5%) and the 256 preset gates toggling with the Sobol.

**Correctness.**
- The SC datapath is bit-identical.
- With int_mode=0 the Sobol sequences and comparators are unchanged, and ring_q resets to 0.
- SC resumes after the usual Sobol reset.
designs.correctness_argument:
1. **Lane.** For every k, every |d_a| in 0..2 and every |d_w| in 0..8, the comparator outputs give |A&W| = |d_a||d_w|; this is checked exhaustively on both banks. With the gate-level PaynPopcount16Csa and the XOR / -16N identity, every signed digit pair (8 lanes x 85 pairs) yields d_a*d_w.
2. **Cycle.** |sum_k d_a d_w| <= 8*16 = 128 = K*M, the same bound as SC.
   - So low_sum = acc_low + d stays in [-128, 639], which means exactly one borrow or one carry.
   - The lazy +-1 acc_high therefore stays valid.
3. **Ring.**
   - Canonical acc_out folds the pending flags, and shift_in clears them.
   - x4 is pure wiring, exact iff 4*value fits in 24 bits.
   - Worst-case register bounds over all digit partial sums give these chunk limits:
     - INT8 FH: 511
     - INT8 HY/HYS: 8191, since |a*d_w| <= 1024
     - W4A8: 8191
     - INT4: 131071
   - Check for FH: 511*16384 = 8,372,224 < 2^23.
4. **Horner.**
   - After pass p, X = sum_k sum_{p'>=p} 4^(p'-p) d_a[p'] d_w[q].
   - After p=0, X = sum_k a_k d_w[q], because sum_p 4^p d_a[p] = a.
   - Output: sum_q 16^q X_q = sum_k a_k w_k.
5. **Grid.**
   - ring_q makes the same one-edge hop as a_bits_pipe, so PE(r,c) rotates exactly on the 8 idle slots at edges s+r+c+2.
   - Global drains start at s_last+P_R+P_C+1, after the far PE's last accumulate. The next segment starts when PE(0,0) can no longer collide with the drain.
6. **Collector.** It works in >= 32 bits, since |out| <= 2^14*K.
designs.model_result:
Full run is in model_weight_outer_horner.log: 9.3 s, exit 0, ALL CHECKS PASSED.

**What is modelled.** Edge by edge:
- edge held registers, and the unchanged comparators with the preset and the real masks;
- PE bit and sign pipes, load_*_sign_q, ring_q and the ring mux;
- 64 tiles per PE with gate-level counters, per-lane XOR, the -16N row, the DW02 sum mod 2^11, the LOW_W=9 low segment, pending carry/borrow, the lazy 15-bit high and canonical acc_out;
- the global drain and the east collector;
- P_R x P_C grids with skewed feeds and the travelling ring_q.

**Checks on every edge.**
- The canonical accumulator must equal an independent digit-level shadow value. This catches any datapath error and any OW24 wrap.
- |acc| < 2^23.
- low_sum must be inside [-128, 1023] and equal to the true sum.
- Pending carry and borrow are never both set.
- Final output must equal numpy int64 A@W.

**121 GEMM cases pass.**
- Main sweep: INT8, W4A8 and INT4 x {FH, HY, HYS, GD, LSB}.
  - K = 8, 64 and 1024 with random full-range data; rows are forced to -128/127 (INT8) or -8/7 (INT4).
  - K = 64 with all-max, all-min, min x max and alternating signs.
- Grids 2x2, 2x3 and 3x2 with K from 136 to 1024.
- Chunk-limit edges:
  - FH at K=511 and 1022 with all (-128)(-128): max|acc| 8,372,224.
  - HY and HYS at K=8191 all-min: 8,387,584.
  - W4A8 HY at K=8191 min x max.
  - LSB at K=4096.

**Negative tests, both caught:**
- FH with chunk 512 on all-min data: OW24 wrap flagged at edge 483.
- One corrupted comparator threshold.

**Other passes.** The exhaustive lane check and all 65,536 INT8 pairs as digit sums pass. weight_outer_horner_costs.py confirms its closed-form slot counts equal the model's schedule.

**Not modelled:** the bit-plane variant, the Sobol flops (the bus is modelled as forced) and power.
designs.competitor_comparison:
**Dedicated BOS INT8** (8x8 OS, 15,797 um2 routed, 64 MAC/cycle, 1,620.5 GMAC/s/mm2), sized for the same effective INT8 rate:
- 4x4 at K=4096 (994 MAC/cycle) needs 15.5 BOS arrays = 245,331 um2 = 47.0% of the SC grid. At K=1024 it needs 14.3 arrays (43.2%).
- 4x8 needs 30.5 arrays = 482k um2 (47.5%).
- 1 PE needs 0.98 array (35% of the array).
- W4A8 / INT4 at equal throughput need 491k / 629k um2 of BOS INT8 / INT4 arrays in 4x4.
- This INT mode costs 2,467 um2 (0.47%), or 5,014 um2 (0.96%) with the collector.
- Standalone, BOS is 2.1x more area-efficient for INT8 (1,620 vs 758 GMAC/s/mm2), but all of its area idles in SC mode. A single small BOS (3% of a 4x4) gives only 64 MAC/cycle, 6.4% of this mode's rate. Reuse wins unless INT is most of the MACs.

**All digits in space (the other angle):**
- Same zero tile cost, and 2.7x less operand traffic per PE (6.75 vs 18 b/MAC).
- But each output block lasts only K/8 cycles and leaves 8 digit-sums per output, so the global drain (38 slots in 4x4, 74 in 4x8) is paid 8x as often.
- INT8 4x4: 0.626 / 0.771 / 0.931 against 0.866 / 0.892 / 0.971 MAC/cycle/tile here, at K = 511 / 1024 / 4096.
- It catches up only at K >= 16k in 4x4 and 4x8, and roughly ties at 1 PE.
- If the spatial design gets overlapped drains or one drain exit per PE column, it regains the lead without re-streaming.

**Bit-plane under the same weight-outer order** (W planes in space, A planes in time, x2 ring):
- Beats Booth from K ~ 1,272 (4x4) or ~1,744 (4x8). At K=4096 in 4x4 it reaches 1.46 vs 0.97 MAC/cycle/tile (1,136 GMAC/s/mm2).
- It needs 1,024 bits per side per cycle (2x the ports) and a 1,024-OR comparator bypass per edge half, +1.09% of 4x4 in total with the ring.
- I would treat it as the upgrade if the memory system can feed it. The Booth lane family is the baseline because it fits the existing ports.
designs.verdict_on_user_shift_down_idea:
**Verdict.** It works only as a shift once per pass in weight-outer order, not every cycle. Even then, shifting up beats it.

**How it was modelled.** Bit-exact as the LSB variant.
- Same ring hardware, wired as an arithmetic >>2.
- Digits go least significant first. After each pass the low 2 bits of every tile are final and leave at the PE's west edge, inside the grid.

**The storage problem.**
- Those bits must be kept: 2 bits per tile per rotation is 640 bits per PE for INT8 (878 um2/PE). With the ring that totals 3.17% of a 4x4 grid.
- It also needs a readout path to the collector, which does not exist.

**Its one advantage is range.**
- The tile holds result>>10, so there is no 511-MAC chunking and only one drain per block.
- 4x4 INT8 at K=1024: 0.929 vs 0.892 MAC/cycle/tile. That is +4% INT throughput for +2.7% area that SC mode also pays.

**Shifting down every cycle (reduction-outer) breaks PaYN's output-stationary accumulator.**
- Bits shifted out in one block would have to be merged back when the next block adds at weight 2^0.
- That needs a rotating 24-bit register and in-tile shift muxes (>= 9.9 um2/tile, 2% of the grid), and it breaks the lazy +-1 high segment.

**Recommendation.** Shift up (MSB-first) between passes using the zero-tile drain ring.
risks: Operand bandwidth: weight-outer re-sends every operand once per digit pass (8x for INT8, 4x W4A8, 2x INT4). The existing 512+64-bit ports suffice exactly, but SRAM must supply 576 bits per edge side every cycle (4,608 b/cycle in 4x4, 8x SC's average); otherwise INT throughput falls proportionally.

The comparator preset depends on the compile-time scramble strides and salts (159, 99, 0/128) and on M=16. Any change needs a re-search; search_booth_comparator_preset.py finds a preset on its first restart. SC must restart from a Sobol reset after INT mode.
OW24 range: FH is exact only for chunks of at most 511 INT8 MACs per drain, and HYS for at most 8191. Longer reductions need output read-modify-write in the memory system.
Timing is not verified. The ring_q OR on shift_in adds one gate to today's WNS path (+0.146 ns). The ~170 um ring return on tile column 0's acc_in path is estimated at about 1 ns of 2.5 ns.

The win over all-digits-in-space rests on the global-drain model (MACs lost during shift_in, a chain of P_C*8 slots). Overlapped drains or one drain exit per PE column would remove most of that advantage.
Grid feed skew (the r/c delay of operands and ring_in) is needed in INT as in SC; it is still bench-only and not in the composite area.
INT-mode power is unmeasured: the edge registers (1,152 bits/PE), the sign pipes and the -16N row toggle every cycle.
All areas are cell-count estimates (MXT2 ring rows, AND/OR preset forcing, collector), not synthesized. The collector belongs to the memory system and is not in today's composite.

designs.name: Spatial Booth digit grid: fixed-weight tiles with a fixed-shift combine at the east edge (no tile change)
designs.angle: No shifting inside tiles. Each tile accumulates digit products of a single fixed weight 4^p*16^q for the whole output block. The weights are applied once per output, by shift-add, where the drain chain leaves the grid. Bit-plane all-space (BISMO in space) is the other member of this family and is evaluated alongside.
designs.plain_summary: Don't shift inside the tile: give every tile one fixed binary weight and apply the weights once, as results drain out. Split a into 4 radix-4 Booth digits, da[p] = -2*a bit(2p+1) + a bit(2p) + a bit(2p-1), each in [-2,2]. Split w into 2 radix-16 digits dw[q] in [-8,8]. Tile row h = (activation, p), column v = (weight, q). Each cycle lane k carries one digit pair. a_bits[k][m] lights 8|da| of the 16 positions and w_bits[k][m] lights 2|dw| positions placed so that count[k] = |da|*|dw| <= 16, with sign[k] = sign(da)^sign(dw). The unchanged tile ends a block holding out_pq = sum_k da[p]*dw[q]. At the east edge, out = sum 4^p*16^q*out_pq. The unchanged comparators produce these bits once the Sobol bus is parked at constants found by search. Rates: INT8 1, W4A8 2, INT4 4 MAC/cycle/tile. Cost is 0.4-1.9% of a 4x4 grid, all at the edges.
designs.mapping:
The same RTL handles all modes; only the operand feed and the combiner grouping change.

INT8 x INT8 (8 digit pairs per MAC):
- PE row h = 4i+p: activation i in {0,1}, a-digit p in 0..3.
- PE column v = 2j+q: weight j in 0..3, w-digit q in {0,1}.
- At slice s, lane k carries reduction index 8s+k.
- The A port byte (i,k) is the raw INT8 a[i][8s+k]. The edge recoder computes x1 = b(2p+1)^b(2p), x0 = b(2p)^b(2p-1), nz = x1|x0, two = x1&~x0.
- The code loaded into a_binary_q[h][k] is pure wiring: code bit = C1[k] bit ? nz : two. C1 = {173,115,122,124,119,130,113,129} and C2 = 255.
- a_sign[k] = raw bit 2p+1.
- W radix-16 digit: dw_q = -8b(4q+3) + 4b(4q+2) + 2b(4q+1) + b(4q) + b(4q-1). Then w_binary_q[v][k] = CODE_W[k][|dw_q|] (a 9-entry per-lane table) and w_sign[k] = bit 4q+3.
- The comparator (bit = code > preset[m]^MASK(k,m)) with Sobol bus presets PRESET_A/W (sweeps/int_mode/search_booth_presets.py) gives:
  - a_bits[k][m] = |da| > r_k(m), where row r_k(m) = 0 for the 8 lowest A thresholds;
  - w_bits[k][m] = |dw| > c_k(m), where column c_k(m) is the rank pair of the W threshold, and each rank pair holds exactly one row-0 position.
  So popcount(a_bits[k] & w_bits[k]) = |da|*|dw| exactly. Certified for all k, both banks, all digit values and sign pairs.
- Tile (h,v) accumulates out_pq(i,j) = sum_k da_p(a[i][k]) * dw_q(w[k][j]).
- PE output block: 2 activations x 4 weights = 8 outputs (SC: 64). A 4x4 grid gives an 8x16 output tile (SC: 32x32).

W4A8:
- A as INT8.
- Each W port byte j packs nibbles {w(2j+1), w(2j)}. The recoder's q=1 b(-1) input is forced to 0, so dw = w (|w| <= 8, sign = w bit 3).
- PE column v is weight v directly: 8 weights, 16 outputs per PE.

INT4 x INT4:
- Each A byte i packs {a(2i+1), a(2i)}.
- Rows h = 4i+p: p in {0,1} carry the 2 radix-4 digits of a(2i); p in {2,3} carry those of a(2i+1). One AND gate forces b(-1)=0 for digit 2.
- W as W4A8. 4 activations x 8 weights = 32 outputs per PE.

Bit-plane all-space (option only, not recommended as the primary mapping):
- PE row = a-plane, column = w-plane, tile sign = (pa==7)^(pw==7), with 128 different k per tile per cycle.
- 2/4/8 MAC/cycle/tile peak for INT8/W4A8/INT4.
- It needs 1024 fresh bits per edge half per cycle, so the comparators must be bypassed (1024 OR2 per half plus a new 1024-bit port).
designs.schedule:
Loop order: grid output tile outer; reduction slices s = 0..S-1 inner, with S = L/8. All digit pairs run in parallel in space, so there is no digit loop in time and no re-streaming.

Feed: edge row r receives A slice s at cycle F+s+r, and edge column c receives W slice s at cycle F+s+c. This is the usual systolic skew; zero padding outside the window gives exactly 0 for any sign.

Control: load_a, load_w, load_a_sign and load_w_sign are held at 1 and rng_en at 0. mac_en is high for S + (P_R + P_C - 2) edges, then shift_in for 8*P_C edges. The next block's first MAC edge follows the drain directly.

Cycles per output block = L/8 + (P_R + P_C - 2) + 8*P_C. One PE: L/8 + 8. 4x4: L/8 + 38. 4x8 drained along 8 columns: L/8 + 74 (drained along 4: L/8 + 42).

Utilisation (simulated cycle counts equal this formula):
- 1 PE: 0.889 / 0.941 / 0.985 / 0.994 at L = 512 / 1024 / 4096 / 11008.
- 4x4: 0.627 / 0.771 / 0.931 / 0.973.
- 4x8 (P_C=8): 0.464 / 0.634 / 0.874 / 0.949.
- 8x4: 0.604 / 0.753 / 0.924 / 0.970.

Accumulator contents:
- After MAC edge n of the block, tile (h=(i,p), v=(j,q)) of PE (r,c) holds acc = sum over k < 8(n - r - c) of da_p*dw_q.
- After the window it holds out_pq(i,j). Pending carry and borrow are folded into the canonical acc_out, as in SC.
- Drain edge d samples acc_out_east from PE column P_C-1-floor(d/8), tile column v = 7-(d mod 8). After 8*P_C edges all tiles are 0, so no clear is needed.
- Combiner stage 1: P_t = v[2t] + 4*v[2t+1]; Q_u = P_2u + 16*P_2u+1 = sum_p 4^p * out_pq.
- Stage 2 (INT8): on the q=1 drain cycle R <= Q; on the q=0 cycle OUT <= 16*R + Q = sum_{p,q} 4^p 16^q out_pq = sum_k a[i][k]*w[k][j].
- W4A8 emits Q; INT4 emits P.
designs.shift_mechanism:
There is no shift in any tile; the tile RTL is untouched.

All 2^s weighting happens once per output in the east-edge combiner, one per PE row, fed by the existing acc_out_east drain stream (24 bits x 8 rows per cycle):
- Stage-1 registers: four 27-bit adders P_t = v[2t] + (v[2t+1] << 2), then two 32-bit adders Q_u = P_2u + (P_2u+1 << 4).
- Stage 2: on the q=1 drain cycle R <= Q (2 x 32-bit); on the q=0 cycle OUT <= (R << 4) + Q (2 x 36-bit).
- The q pair is a one-step Horner (shift by 4) on the drain stream. The user's shifter exists, but at the edge, once per output, on 2 values.
- Roughly 220 FA, 200 flops and glue: about 741 um2 per PE row.

Pending carry/borrow interaction: none new. The per-cycle tile range is exactly SC's (|d| <= K*M = 128), so the LOW_W=9 low segment, the pending carry/borrow flags and the lazy +-1 acc_high work unchanged. The drain reads the canonical acc_out (high_next with pending folded in), and shift_in clears pending, as in SC.

Because tiles hold unweighted digit-product sums (|acc| <= 16L), OWIDTH=24 suffices up to L = 524,287. Only the edge combiner is wide (36 bits).

Contrast: any scheme that keeps the weighted INT8 sum in the tile (in-tile Horner, drain-ring Horner, LSB-first shift-down, or the thermometer mapping with Horner) overflows OW24 for L > 511 in the worst case (-128*-128). It needs OW=28 at L=4096 and 29 at L=11008, at +3.724 um2 per bit per tile.

The combine can also be done downstream (0 grid area), at the price of 8x more drained values per output.
designs.sign_handling:
Inputs are two's complement INT8/INT4; the full range including -128 and -8 is handled, with -128 giving da3 = -2 and dw1 = -8.

Each lane carries one signed digit pair, so the existing per-lane sign gives the product sign: sign[k] = a_sign[k] ^ w_sign[k].
- a_sign = raw bit 2p+1; w_sign = raw bit 4q+3. Both are wires, with zero gates.
- A digit equal to 0 with sign bit 1 (bit patterns 111 or 11111) is harmless. Its count is 0 and the CSA trick gives (0^1) on the 5 counter bits = 16, then -16 = 0 exactly.
- The tile's 5 sign XORs per lane and the one -16*countones(neg) correction row are used as-is.
- The peripheral sign registers and the PE sign pipes reload every cycle: load_a/load_w and load_a_sign/load_w_sign are held high. The sign-pipe enables already exist.
- The -16N row and the sign pipes toggle every cycle in INT mode, where SC holds them for a block. This affects energy only.
- No two's-complement plane signs are needed, except in the optional bit-plane mapping, where the tile sign is the constant (pa==7)^(pw==7).

rtl_changes.change: None. inner_tile_signed_segmented_csa.sv is unchanged: same AND/CSA/sign-XOR/-16N heap, LOW_W=9, pending carry/borrow, OWIDTH=24 and drain mux.
None. Bit pipes already capture every clock; sign pipes already reload when load_*_sign_q=1, which is held high in INT mode; re-export rails unchanged.

A edge half (per PE row): radix-4 Booth recoder producing nz/two per digit lane, with the 8-bit code wired from nz/two using per-lane constants C1[k]; INT4 gating of digit-2 b(-1); 2:1 merge in front of a_binary_q (code vs SC magnitude) and a_signs_q (digit sign vs SC sign). Comparators untouched.

W edge half (per PE column), raw weights: radix-16 |digit| from 5 bits, per-lane 9-entry code LUT CODE_W[k][|dw|], W4 gating, 512-bit code merge and 64-bit sign merge into w_binary_q/w_signs_q. If weights are pre-coded offline (8-bit code + sign per digit, 2.25x INT weight storage) this is 0 um2; storing sign+|digit| (1.25x) makes it 740.7 um2. Raw is required for activation x activation GEMMs such as QK^T.

Shared Sobol pair (one per grid): synchronous preset of the 2x128 random_value flops to the constants PRESET_A/PRESET_W, held with rng_en=0. The gate sits in the flop D path, off the +0.307 ns Sobol-Q -> comparator -> bit-pipe path. Masks are untouched.

East-edge output combiner per PE row on acc_out_east: stage 1 has four 27-bit and two 32-bit fixed-shift adders; stage 2 has the q-pair Horner (R<<4)+Q at 36 bits; mode select for INT8/W4A8/INT4 and an SC bypass mux. Optional: the combine can be done downstream for 0 um2.

int_mode and precision CSR (2 bits); one-cycle preset pulse; hold load_a/load_w/load_a_sign/load_w_sign=1 and rng_en=0; mac_en window of S+P_R+P_C-2 and shift_in of 8*P_C per block; combiner q-phase toggle. Not included in the totals.

Data mover feeds raw two's-complement bytes on the existing 512-bit binary ports (INT8: 16 A bytes per PE-row edge and 32 W bytes per PE-column edge per cycle), packs INT4/W4 nibble pairs, and applies the r/c skew. The skew also exists for SC but lives only in the bench today. 1536 b/cycle into a 4x4 grid versus 576 average in SC.

area.arithmetic: Per-edge parts from LEF cell areas: A half 533.1, W half (raw) 1217.4, Sobol preset 112.9 per grid, combiner 740.9 per PE row. Grid areas: routed u_pe 29,255.548 and periph 13,031.256, composite = P_R*P_C*u_pe + (P_R+P_C)*periph/2 + Sobol pair. Single PE (routed 44,017.974): 533.1 + 1217.4 + 112.9 + 740.9 = 2,604.3 um2 = 5.92%. 4x4 (521,892): 4x533.1 + 4x1217.4 + 112.9 + 4x740.9 = 2,132.4 + 4,869.6 + 112.9 + 2,963.6 = 10,078.5 um2 = 1.93%, so SC efficiency goes from 784.8 to 770.0 GMAC/s/mm2. 4x8 (P_R=4, P_C=8; 1,016,043): 4x533.1 + 8x1217.4 + 112.9 + 4x740.9 = 14,948 um2 = 1.47% (806.3 to 794.6). 8x4 (the drain-friendly orientation): 15,175 um2 = 1.49%. Lean config (W pre-coded offline, combine downstream): 1 PE 646 (1.47%); 4x4 4x533.1 + 112.9 = 2,245 (0.43%, SC 781.5); 4x8 2,245 (0.22%). Middle config (W stored as sign+|digit|, combiner in grid): 4x4 8,172 (1.57%). Tile area added is 0, so nothing scales with the 1,024 (4x4) or 2,048 (4x8) tile copies. These are cell-count estimates, not synthesis; the recoder LUT and combiner carry about +-30%.

throughput.notes:
Peak rates equal SC's 1 MAC/cycle/tile for INT8, and 2x and 4x SC for W4A8 and INT4. 8 lanes x 1 digit pair per lane per cycle; INT8 needs 8 pairs per MAC, W4A8 4, INT4 2. Every precision shares the drain utilisation (L/8)/(L/8 + P_R + P_C - 2 + 8*P_C). 4x4, full self-contained config (531,971 um2):
- INT8: peak 770.0 GMAC/s/mm2; 483 / 594 / 717 / 749 at L = 512 / 1024 / 4096 / 11008.
- W4A8: peak 1540; 966 / 1187 / 1434 / 1499.
- INT4: peak 3080; 1933 / 2375 / 2867 / 2997.
For reference, the BOS dedicated arrays reach 1620 (INT8) and 2491 (INT4). A 1 PE array runs at 94% utilisation at L=1024; the drain bubble only grows with P_C, so drain along the short grid side. The optional bit-plane all-space mapping (also zero tile change) has a 2x higher INT8 peak but 64 tiles per output. It overtakes the Booth grid only for L > ~4,260 at 4x4 (1073 vs 749 GMAC/s/mm2 at L=11008) and needs 1024-bit ports per edge half and 4 b/MAC.

bandwidth.notes: These are raw two's-complement operand bits. INT8 per PE: A 2 activations x 8 k x 8 b = 128 b/cycle plus W 4 weights x 8 k x 8 b = 256 b/cycle, so 384 b/cycle = 6.0 b/MAC on one PE. In a 4x4 grid, 4x128 + 4x256 = 1536 b/cycle for 1024 MAC/cycle = 1.5 b/MAC. W4A8: 384 b/cycle per PE (3.0 b/MAC); 4x4 1536 (0.75 b/MAC). INT4: 384 (1.5 b/MAC); 4x4 1536 (0.375 b/MAC). SC for reference: 144 b/cycle per PE (2.25 b/MAC); 4x4 576 (0.5625 b/MAC). INT8 therefore needs 2.67x SC's edge bandwidth. The existing 512-bit binary and 64-bit sign ports per edge half suffice; the port carries 128 or 256 raw bits per cycle, recoded at the edge. Pre-coded W fills the 512-bit W port exactly (512 + 64 b/cycle per edge). Re-read factor 1: no digit pass re-streams any operand. Temporal Horner variants re-stream 8x: 4.0 b/MAC raw at 4x4, or 2.0 with digit-plane memory layouts. The cost of the spatial layout is output reuse. The output tile shrinks from 32x32 (SC, 4x4) to 8x16 (INT8), so in a large GEMM A is fetched 2x and W 4x more often than in SC. In exchange, batch-1 GEMV keeps 50% of rows busy versus 12.5% in SC.

designs.sc_mode_impact:
Area:
- Full self-contained config: +10.08k um2 in 4x4 (1.93%); SC efficiency 784.8 to 770.0 GMAC/s/mm2.
- 4x8: +1.47% (806.3 to 794.6). Single PE: +5.92% (581.6 to 549.1), because the edge cost is not amortised.
- Lean config (W pre-coded offline, combine downstream): +0.43% in 4x4 (781.5) and +0.22% in 4x8.
- Nothing is added per tile, so nothing scales with the 64, 1,024 or 2,048 tile copies.

Tile critical path: unchanged; the tile RTL is untouched.
- The routed WNS endpoints (shift_in to the acc_high ICG, +0.146 ns) and the Sobol-Q to comparator to w_bits_pipe path (+0.307 ns) gain no new logic.
- The Sobol preset gate sits in the random_value D path, a Sobol-internal path.
- The A/W merge AO22s sit after the input port, before a_binary_q (an input-delay path, about +60 ps).
- The combiner sits after acc_out_east, with an SC bypass mux on the output.
- INT mode exercises only existing single-cycle tile paths with the same per-cycle range.

Power:
- In SC, the edge recoders see the SC magnitude data toggle unless their inputs are gated by int_mode (about +0.15k um2 to gate). The combiner is bypassed. This is otherwise negligible.
- In INT mode, the held registers, the sign pipes and the -16N row toggle every cycle (unmeasured).

Correctness: with int_mode=0, every merge and the preset are transparent, so SC streams and drained values are bit-identical by construction. The existing SC bit-exact benches must be rerun after the RTL edit to confirm.
designs.correctness_argument:
Digit identity: for two's complement, a = sum_p 4^p * da_p (radix-4 Booth, 4 digits for INT8 and 2 for INT4) and w = sum_q 16^q * dw_q (radix-16 Booth, 2 digits for INT8 and 1 for 4-bit w). Exact for every value including -128 and -8 (model part 1, all pairs).

Lane: the comparator ranking property makes popcount(a_bits & w_bits) = |da|*|dw| <= 16 = M for every lane k, every digit pair and every sign pair (model part 0).

Sign: lane = sum(bits^n)*weights - 16n = (n ? -count : count). A zero count gives exactly 0 for any sign bit, so the digit-zero patterns 111 and 11111 and the skew zero padding are harmless.

Range and overflow:
- Per cycle |d| = |sum_k lane| <= K*M = 128, identical to SC. So low_sum = acc_low + d lies in [-128, 639], inside signed SUM_W = 11 bits. Negative means exactly one borrow and bit 9 means exactly one carry, so the pending flags and the lazy +-1 acc_high stay valid. The model asserts this every cycle and also checks that the 11-bit heap sum never wraps.
- Tile magnitude: |acc| <= 128 per cycle x L/8 cycles = 16L < 2^23 for L <= 524,287. The largest seen in the model is 65,536 (all -128, L=4096).
- Combiner: |out| <= 2^14 * L, so 36 bits covers L <= 2^19. Intermediate P (27 b) and Q (32 b) hold any 24-bit tile values.

Drain: shift_in has priority, loads the canonical acc_out (pending folded) and clears pending, so drained values are exact. Zero fill leaves every tile at 0 for the next block. The model checks two back-to-back blocks.

Skew: A and W slices meet in PE (r,c) at F+s+r+c+2, as in SC, and mac_en covers the whole skewed window.

The model also asserts every cycle that the canonical acc_out equals an exact integer shadow sum and that pending carry and borrow are never both set.
designs.model_result:
Full run: python3 sweeps/int_mode/model_spatial_fixed_weight.py takes 3.6 s; log in sweeps/int_mode/model_spatial_fixed_weight.log. Result: ALL CHECKS PASSED.

- Part 0: the Sobol-bus presets are certified. For all 8 lanes, both banks, |da| = 0..2, |dw| = 0..8 and all 4 sign pairs, the real comparator, gate-level PaynPopcount16Csa, sign XOR and -16N produce exactly da*dw.
- Part 1: every value pair is exact through recoder, comparator, lane and digit weights: INT8xINT8 (65,536), INT8xINT4 (4,096), INT4xINT4 (256).
- Part 2: 86 full GEMM runs through the register-level grid model, 7,920 outputs, all bit-exact against numpy int64.
  - Coverage: modes INT8, W4A8 and INT4; L = 8, 64, 1024 on 1x1 and 2x2 grids, L = 4096 on 1x1, L = 64 on 4x4.
  - Data: random full range, all max (127/7), all min (-128/-8), alternating signs, mixed extremes; two back-to-back output blocks per run.
  - What the model includes: edge recoders, the comparators with constant presets and real masks, PE bit and sign pipes with re-export and load_*_sign_q, systolic skew, the tile's 11-bit heap mod 2^11, the LOW_W=9 low segment with pending carry/borrow and lazy acc_high, global mac_en/shift_in, the drain chain, and the 2-stage east-edge combiner.

  - Measured cycles per block equal the formula.

Supporting scripts:
- sweeps/int_mode/model_spatial_fixed_weight_mutations.py injects 5 faults (drop the -16N row, a threshold crossing the code cut, a wrong W code, LOW_W=7, W sign pipes never loaded). All 5 are reported, and a benign threshold change is correctly not flagged.
- sweeps/int_mode/search_booth_presets.py reproduces the presets by annealing in both bank orientations. No native Sobol state works (best has 20 violations), and a k-independent binned code was not found, so per-lane code tables are needed.
designs.competitor_comparison:
Dedicated BOS INT8 with equal INT throughput:
- The 4x4 INT8 peak is 1024 MAC/cycle, which takes 16 BOS arrays: 16 x 15,797 = 252,758 um2 = +48.4% of the grid.
- SC efficiency drops to 528.8 GMAC/s/mm2, against 770.0 with this INT mode (full config) or 781.5 (lean config).
- The whole BOS-augmented chip delivers INT8 at 528.8 GMAC/s/mm2 even at 100% utilisation. PaYN's INT mode gives 717 at L=4096 and 594 at L=1024.

Equal added area: the 10.08k um2 spent here buys 0.64 of one BOS array, about 41 INT8 MAC/cycle (16 GMAC/s). This mode gives 1024 peak (about 953 effective at L=4096), roughly 23x more INT8 throughput per added um2.

Mixed workloads with 10% of MACs in INT:
- Run sequentially, this mode reaches 764 GMAC/s/mm2, while a right-sized sidecar of 1.78 BOS (+5.4%) reaches about 414 because one array always sits idle.
- A sidecar wins (about 827) only if SC and INT layers can run concurrently, which needs layer pipelining and extra SRAM bandwidth.

Pure-INT silicon: BOS (1620 INT8, 2491 INT4) remains about 2x better. This mode is a reuse feature, not a competitive INT engine.

Other no-or-low tile-cost alternatives at 4x4 INT8, all charged the same edge recoders:
- Drain-ring Horner (zero tile logic, edge <<2): only valid for L <= 511 at OW=24. With OW=28 it costs +4.93% of the grid (SC 748.0) for 612 / 709 GMAC/s/mm2 at L = 1024 / 4096, and 4 b/MAC. Dominated.
- In-tile x4 Horner (+10.4 um2/tile plus OW widening to 28 bits): +6.71% of the grid (SC 735.5), giving 706 / 728 at L = 1024 / 4096. It wins INT8 at short L but loses about 4.5% of SC efficiency, which violates the SC-first priority.
- Bit-plane all-space: the same angle, 1.5%, wins only for L > ~4.3k.
designs.verdict_on_user_shift_down_idea:
Your intuition is right: INT is "bit products summed, weighted by 2^i". But you don't need a shifter in the tile, and shifting results down every cycle is the costliest place to put the weights.

Here a fixed weight per tile replaces the per-cycle shift. The binary weights are applied once per output, as values leave through the drain chain. That chain is the place where results already shift out, one tile per cycle. The only "shift" left is the edge combiner's (R<<4)+Q on 2 values and fixed wiring offsets (<<2, <<4).

An LSB-first right-shifting tile accumulator would need:
(a) weight-outer passes over the whole reduction, because an emitted low bit is final only once all contributions of that weight are in. Operands would be re-streamed 8 times (4 b/MAC at 4x4 versus 1.5).
(b) per-tile storage for the ~10 emitted bits, plus a right-shift source on all 24 accumulator flops, plus a pending-carry flush cycle at the acc_low/acc_high boundary. That is about 9.4 + 13.7 = 23 um2 per tile, about 4.5% of a 4x4 grid paid in SC mode too.
(c) with reduction-outer order (weight changing every cycle), a rotating accumulator ring instead.
(d) like every scheme that keeps the weighted INT8 sum inside the tile, a wider accumulator. INT8 overflows OWIDTH=24 for L > 511 in the worst case, needing about +15-19 um2 per tile more.

The spatial mapping gives the same arithmetic exactly, at 1 MAC/cycle/tile for INT8, with zero tile change. Shifting down every cycle is dominated; don't build it.
risks: Short reductions: the 8*P_C-cycle drain bubble is paid per output block every L/8 cycles. Utilisation in 4x4 is 63% at L=512 and 77% at L=1024; in 4x8 drained along 8 columns it is 46% and 63%. Orient grids so the drain runs along the short side (8x4: 60% and 75%). If INT layers are mostly short-L, a post-heap {0,2} shift (+11.9 um2/tile per the prior-art estimate, +2.3% of 4x4) lifts L=1024 4x4 utilisation from 77% to about 87%, at the price of SC area.

The comparator-reuse presets depend on the exact compile-time scramble masks (strides 159/99, salts 0/128) and on K=8. Any mask or K change requires rerunning search_booth_presets.py and the model. Bank roles are fixed (A = 3-level radix-4, W = 9-level). Swapping operand roles needs the second preset set that was found, making the preset gate a 3:1 select (about +0.1k um2 per grid).

All area numbers are cell-count estimates, not synthesis. The W recoder LUT (5.4 um2/lane) and the combiner (741 um2/PE row) carry about +-30%. The combiner's 27+32-bit adds in one stage may need another pipeline register at 400 MHz (+64 flops, about 88 um2 per PE row).
Edge cost is not negligible on small arrays: 5.9% of a single PE (1.5% in the lean config). It reaches the 0.4-1.9% range only at grid scale.

Operand bandwidth: INT8 needs 1536 b/cycle into a 4x4 grid, 2.67x SC's 576. Output tiles shrink from 32x32 to 8x16, so in a large GEMM W is fetched 4x and A 2x more often than in SC. The SRAM and data mover must sustain this, and must implement the r/c skew, which today exists only in the bench.

The weight-format choice matters. Pre-coding W offline removes 4.9k um2 (4x4) but costs 2.25x INT weight storage and cannot be used for activation x activation GEMMs (QK^T, AV). The raw-W edge recoder is the safe default.

INT-mode power is unmeasured. a_binary_q (async-reset flops), the sign registers, the sign pipes and the -16N correction row toggle every cycle instead of once per block, and the PE sign-pipe ICGs stay open. Measure this before quoting energy.

Limits: a single output block must have L <= 524,287 (24-bit tiles), and the combiner is sized for L <= 2^19. The interface accepts two's complement only; sign-magnitude +128 is not representable, so the requantizer must emit two's complement.

SC bit-exactness after the RTL edit is argued by construction (int_mode=0 makes the merges and preset transparent). It still has to be confirmed by rerunning the existing SC benches; no EDA was run in this study.

Bit-plane all-space (same angle, zero tile change) beats this mapping for INT8 when L > ~4.3k (1073 vs 749 GMAC/s/mm2 at L=11008, 4x4). It needs 1024-bit fresh-bit ports per edge half plus a comparator bypass. Worth revisiting if long-reduction INT layers dominate.

designs.name: Comparator-native spatial Booth INT (CNSB): unchanged tile and peripheral, Sobol preset, digit weights applied once at the east edge; bit-plane turbo evaluated as the red-team alternative
designs.angle:
Red team. I tried to beat the Booth all-space mapping. Ideas tried: bit-plane with every plane pair in space; weighting inside the heap; NAF and other signed-digit codes; deterministic SC streams; the T loop; splitting M across weights; reusing the -16N row. I also tried to make the edge cheaper by reusing the SC comparators instead of adding inject gates. Then I stress-tested the lead's framing and the BOS alternative.

Result: no angle beats Booth all-space for the tile mapping. Prior_art's mapping wins on mapping. It is optimal among one-product-per-lane codes: radix-4 x radix-16 needs 16 slots per lane and 8 pairs, so INT8 runs at 1 MAC/cycle/tile; radix-8 x radix-8 gives 0.89 and the lead's thermometer gives 0.5.

My contributions:
(a) A comparator-native edge. A searched preset of the 16 Sobol values per side makes the unchanged comparators emit the Booth 2x8 thermometers. That puts 101 um2 inside the grid composite, against 3.2k for OR injection, and adds nothing to the +0.307 ns path.
(b) Bit-plane with all 64 plane pairs in space needs no tile change and reaches 2/4/8 MAC/cycle/tile, the ceiling for one bit product per slot. But it costs 4 b/MAC on a 4x4 grid, and with 128 k per cycle per output the 8*P_C drain dominates. It beats Booth only for L above about 4.3k (4x4) or about 9k (4x8).
(c) The drain, not the arithmetic, limits INT at grid scale.

Verdicts on the lead's framing:
- (i)A's 16-cycle bound is refuted.
- (i)B's 2048 b/cycle per PE is true per PE but is 4 b/MAC on a 4x4 grid. It needs no tile shifter if the planes are put in space.
- (ii) With weights in space there is no weight loop at all.
- (iii) Shift-down is dominated.
- "Ramp replaces random values" fails for the 2x8 grid: the ramp gives a threshold of 255 and the wrong pairing. A searched preset plus per-lane codes is required. No lane-independent code table and no wiring-only radix-16 encoder turned up in the search (best runs still had 6-9 and 24 violations).
designs.plain_summary: Keep the tile as it is and put the bit weights in space, not in time. Split a into 4 radix-4 Booth digits da[p] (|da|<=2) and w into 2 radix-16 digits dw[q] (|dw|<=8). Give each digit pair its own tile: row h=(i,p), column v=(j,q). Each lane carries one pair on a 2x8 grid of the 16 positions: a_bits[k][m]=(|da|>r(m)) and w_bits[k][m]=(|dw|>c(m)). Then count[k]=|da|*|dw|<=16 and sign[k]=sign(da) XOR sign(dw), which is exactly what the SC tile already computes. Each tile adds up da*dw over k within the SC range, so the accumulator needs no change. The bit weights 2^(2p+4q) are applied once per output at the east edge, where the drain already delivers the q digits most significant first: out=16*H+s. The unchanged comparators make these thermometers once the 16 Sobol values are preset. Throughput is 1 (INT8), 2 (W4A8) and 4 (INT4) MAC/cycle/tile, for 101 um2 inside the grid.
designs.mapping:
**INT8, orientation 'r4rows' (used for 1x1 and 4x4)**
- Tile row h=4i+p: i in {0,1} is the activation row, p in 0..3 is the radix-4 Booth digit of a.
- Tile column v=2j+q: j in 0..3 is the weight column, q in {0,1} is the radix-16 Booth digit of w.
- In cycle t, lane k carries reduction index k'=8t+k.
- Signs: a_sign[h][k] = da_p(a[i,k'])<0 and w_sign[v][k] = dw_q(w[k',j])<0, through the existing sign ports and sign pipes. load_*_sign_in is held at 1, so the sign pipes reload every cycle.
- Positions: per lane there is a bijection m <-> (r,c) in {0,1}x{0..7}, with a_bits[h][k][m]=(|da|>r) and w_bits[v][k][m]=(|dw|>c). So popcount = |da|*|dw| <= 16.

**Edge E2 (proposed)**
- The bijection is set per lane by the preset thresholds: r=1 on the 8 largest row thresholds of lane k, and c = rank/2 among the column thresholds of lane k.
- The feeder writes binary_q[h][k] = E_row[k][|da|], which is one of {0, C_k, 255}, where C_k is the 9th-smallest row threshold of lane k. Each bit of this code is a wire from (|da|>=1) or (|da|==2).
- It writes binary_q[v][k] = E_col[k][|dw|]: 9 per-lane codes, with 0 and 255 at the ends.
- Preset values are in PRESETS in the model.

**Edge E1 (alternative)**
- m = 8r + c. binary_q is held at 0, so the comparators output 0, and the thermometer bits are ORed in after the comparator.

**Output counts**
- INT8: 8 outputs (2x4) per PE, 64 MAC/cycle.
- W4A8: rows 4i+p (2 activation rows x 4 digits), columns v=j (8 weight columns; w in [-8,7] is its own radix-16 digit). 16 outputs, 128 MAC/cycle.
- INT4: rows 2i+p (4 activation rows x 2 radix-4 digits), 8 weight columns. 32 outputs, 256 MAC/cycle.

**4x8 orientation 'r16rows'**
- Activations go on rows as radix-16 digits (4 activation rows per PE). Weights go on columns as radix-4 digits (2 per PE), using the second searched preset.
- This cuts edge traffic to 2048 b/cycle from 2560.

**Grid**
- PE(r,c) owns activation rows NI*r.. and weight columns NJ*c...
- The A edge is skewed by r and the W edge by c, as in the existing systolic wiring. The drain chain runs across PE columns.

**Bit-plane turbo (E1 only)**
- Rows are the 8 two's-complement planes of one activation row; columns are the 8 planes of one weight column.
- All 128 slots of a tile hold distinct k (k' = 128t + 16k + m).
- Sign = 1 on all lanes of plane-7 rows and columns.
- W4A8: columns (j, plane) with j in {0,1}. INT4: rows (i, plane) and columns (j, plane).
designs.schedule:
**Order:** output-stationary, reduction innermost, no weight loop.

**Per output tile, INT8, one PE:** S = L/8 MAC cycles, then 8 drain cycles. In a grid, add (P_R-1)+(P_C-1) skew cycles; the drain is 8*P_C cycles. The next tile's operands are injected during the drain (2-cycle operand latency), so tiles run back to back. The model verified this with 2 output tiles on a 2x3 grid.

**Accumulator state:**
- After MAC cycle t, tile (4i+p, 2j+q) holds T_pq(t) = sum_{k'<8(t+1)} da_p(a[i,k'])*dw_q(w[k',j]).
- It is stored as acc_low plus acc_high plus pending carry/borrow; the canonical acc_out is exact.
- Per cycle |d| <= 128. At the end |T| <= 16L.

**Drain and combine:**
- At each drain edge the east edge samples global column g = 8*P_C-1 down to 0, before the shift.
- Per PE row and group i: s_i = T_0 + 4*T_1 + 16*T_2 + 64*T_3 for that column (fixed-wired adds).
- If q = 1 (that column arrives first): H <- s_i.
- If q = 0: out(i,j) = 16*H + s_i = sum_k' a[i,k']*w[k',j].

**Cycle counts:**
- Single PE: a 2x4 block takes L/8+8 cycles. An 8x8 block takes 8*(L/8+8) = L+64 cycles (SC: L+8).
- 4x4 grid: an 8x16 block takes L/8+6+32 cycles. W4A8 and INT4 use the same cycles per output tile with 2x and 4x the outputs.

**Effective MAC/cycle/tile (model formula):**

| mode | grid | L=128 | L=1024 | L=4096 | L=11008 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Booth INT8 | 4x4 | 0.30 | 0.77 | 0.93 | 0.97 |
| Booth INT8 | 4x8 | 0.18 | 0.63 | 0.87 | 0.95 |
| Booth INT8 | 1x1 | 0.67 | 0.94 | 0.985 | |
| bit-plane INT8 | 4x4 | 0.05 | 0.35 | 0.91 | 1.39 |
| bit-plane INT8 | 4x8 | 0.03 | 0.20 | 0.60 | 1.08 |

The SC reference on 4x4 is 0.77 at L=128 and 0.99 at L=4096.
designs.shift_mechanism:
**There is no shift inside the tile and no per-cycle shift anywhere.**
- The row weights 4^p and column weights 16^q (bit i = 2p+4q) are applied once per output in a combiner at the grid's east edge, where the drain chain already ends.
- Per PE row there are 2 groups:
  - A 5-input 32-bit carry-save tree computes s_i = t_{4i} + (t_{4i+1}<<2) + (t_{4i+2}<<4) + (t_{4i+3}<<6), plus the Horner term.
  - One 32-bit H register: on the q=1 drain step H <- s; on the q=0 step out <- (H<<4) + s.
- The drain order (east first, v = 2j+1 before 2j) is exactly MSB-first Horner, so no reordering buffer is needed.

**Accumulator interaction:**
- The tile's pending carry/borrow never meets the shift: acc_out = {acc_high + pending, acc_low} is canonical, and shift_in clears pending (existing RTL).
- So the combiner sees exact 24-bit two's-complement tile values.
- LOW_W=9 is untouched because the per-cycle partial stays in [-128, 128]. low_sum stays in [-128, 639], so negative means exactly one borrow and bit 9 means exactly one carry.
- For W4A8 and INT4 Booth there is no column digit, so out = sum_p 4^p t (no H register).
- For bit-plane: per tile row, H <- 2H + t over the plane columns (most significant first), then out = sum_i 2^i H_i.
designs.sign_handling:
**Booth digits**
- Each lane gets sign[k] = sign(da) XOR sign(dw), through the existing a/w sign ports and sign pipes, reloaded every cycle.
- A negative lane uses the tile's 5 XORs plus the shared -16*N row. In INT mode that row changes every cycle (energy only); the arithmetic is exact, and a zero digit gives 0 for either sign.
- Two's-complement INT8 [-128,127] uses standard Booth recoding: 4 radix-4 digits and 2 radix-16 digits.

**PaYN sign-magnitude data (sign s, magnitude 0..128)**
- Take the digits of mag's 8-bit pattern and flip every digit sign by (s XOR mag[7]). That is one extra XOR per digit.
- This covers -128..+128 (+128 is one value beyond INT8), verified at L=64 and L=1024.
- W4A8 and INT4 weights are their own radix-16 digit: sign = w<0, |d| = |w|.

**Bit-plane alternative**
- Two's complement only: the sign is 1 on every lane of the plane-7 row/column and 0 elsewhere, so it is constant and is loaded once.
- Sign-magnitude data cannot be used here, because one lane sign covers 16 different k.

rtl_changes.change: None. 128 AND, counters, sign XORs, the -16N row, the heap, LOW_W=9 low segment, pending flags and drain are reused exactly as they are.
None. INT control holds load_a_sign_in=load_w_sign_in=1 so the sign pipes reload every cycle, holds mac_en for L/8+skew cycles and raises shift_in for the 8*P_C drain. All existing ports.

Peak rates compared with SC's 1 MAC/cycle/tile: INT8 1.0x, W4A8 2x, INT4 4x.

Why 1 is the INT8 ceiling for this family: a lane holds one signed digit product, which needs 2^(ra-1)*2^(rw-1) <= 16 slots. Booth radix 4x16 reaches 8 pairs per MAC, i.e. 1 MAC/cycle/tile. Other codes are worse: radix 8x8 gives 0.889, 4x8 gives 0.667, and the lead's bit x unary-nibble gives 0.5.

Bit-plane turbo (E1) peaks at 2/4/8 MAC/cycle/tile, the ceiling when every slot holds one bit product. But each output takes only L/128 cycles. At 4x4 it is behind Booth for L < ~4.3k (L=4096: 0.914 vs 0.931; L=1024: 0.35 vs 0.77) and ahead only for longer reductions (L=11008: 1.39 vs 0.97). At 4x8 the crossover is about 9k. At batch 1, 'r4rows' fills 1/(2*P_R) of the grid. That is 4x better than SC's 1/(8*P_R), but still only 12.5% on 4x4.

**Single PE, INT8 'r4rows'**

- Into the PE pipes: 2,048 bit-pipe bits + 128 sign bits per cycle, the same as SC.

**4x4 grid**

- SC by comparison needs 576 b/cycle = 0.5625 b/MAC, so INT needs 2.67x more operand bandwidth.
- Re-read: for an MxKxN GEMM the 4x4 output tile is 8x16 (SC: 32x32). A is re-read N/16 times (2x SC), W M/8 times (4x SC). Bits per MAC = 8/16 + 8/8 = 1.5.

designs.correctness_argument:
**Lane product**
- Per lane, the comparator outputs are a prefix of that lane's threshold ranking.
- The preset is chosen so that, for every lane k:
  - (1) No threshold equals 255, so a code of 255 sets all 16 bits.
  - (2) The 8 smallest row thresholds S_1 are strictly below the other 8.
  - (3) The column thresholds sorted in pairs have strict pair boundaries.
  - (4) S_1 contains exactly one position from each column pair.
- Then |S_x ∩ T_y| = x*y for x in 0..2 and y in 0..8, so count[k] = |da|*|dw| <= 16 = M. This was checked exhaustively per lane through the actual comparator formula.
- E1 gets the same result from the fixed bijection m = 8r + c.

**Accumulator range**
- The lane sign is the product sign. The XOR on the 5 redundant bits plus the -16N row gives ±count exactly; this was verified at gate level, and a zero digit gives 0 for either sign.
- The per-cycle partial is in [-128, 128], identical to SC. So low_sum stays in [-128, 639], inside the signed 11-bit range [-128, 1023]: negative means exactly one borrow, bit 9 means exactly one carry.
- acc_high moves only by lazy ±1. A carry and a borrow are never pending together, because a cycle sets at most one.

**Overflow**
- Tile |T| <= 16L < 2^23, so L < 524,288 for INT8.
- The combiner is 32-40 bits. It is exact mod 2^32 whenever the final |y| <= 2^14 * L fits.

**Systolic and drain details**
- Skew padding is zero bits, which contribute exactly 0.
- The drain shifts canonical values, which already include pending, and fills with zeros, so accumulators are 0 for the next tile.
- Next-tile injection overlaps the drain safely: the pipes are ungated, and shift_in has priority while no MAC happens.

**Combine**
- sum_{p,q} 4^p 16^q T_pq = sum_k' (sum_p 4^p da_p)(sum_q 16^q dw_q) = sum_k' a*w, by the Booth identity and linearity.
designs.model_result:
PASS: 134 GEMM runs, all bit-exact against numpy int64 GEMM. Runtime is about 2 s.

**What the model covers**
- A register-level, RTL-faithful model of: the peripheral registers and unchanged comparator (with the real masks), the Sobol preset, the PE bit pipes and sign pipes with the registered load wave, the gate-level PaynPopcount16Csa, the 5-bit sign XOR, the -16N row, the 11-bit heap, LOW_W=9 plus pending flags plus the lazy high segment, the canonical acc_out, shift_in priority, the systolic grid with r/c edge skew, the cross-PE drain, and a register-level east combiner.

**Runs**
- Booth E2, INT8/W4A8/INT4:
  - 1x1 at L = 8, 64, 1024.
  - 2x3 grid with 2 back-to-back output tiles at L=64.
- Booth E2 INT8 'r16rows' on a 2x2 grid at L=256.
- Booth E2 INT8 on a 4x4 grid at L=256.
- Booth E2 INT8 on a 2x2 grid at L=4096, all -128. Each tile reaches 65,536 and the outputs reach 2^26.
- Booth E1 INT8 on a 2x2 grid at L=1024.
- Sign-magnitude INT8 including ±128 at L=64 and 1024.
- Bit-plane E1, INT8/W4A8/INT4:
  - 1x1 at L = 8 (padded), 128, 1024.
  - 2x2 at L=256 with 2 tiles.
- Each configuration ran these data cases: random full range (forced to include -128/127 and -8/7), all max, all min, alternating signs, min x max.

**Checks on every edge**
- The 11-bit heap equals the exact sum.
- The RTL range [-K*M, 2^(LOW_W+1)) holds.
- Carry and borrow are never pending together.
- The canonical 24-bit acc_out equals an exact shadow, so any wrap fails the run.
- The combiner stays within 40 bits.
- All accumulators are zero after the drain.

**Presets:** both orientations verified exhaustively per lane (count == |x|*|y|).

**Negative tests (each fires as intended)**
- OWIDTH=14 overflow.
- The Sobol reset state used as the preset.
- One corrupted code-table entry.
- W skew off by one.
- The -16N row dropped.

**Not covered:** the model does not simulate SC-mode streams. SC safety rests on the hardware changes being zero, apart from the preset gate.
designs.competitor_comparison:
**Equal INT throughput.** Booth INT8 on a 4x4 grid is 1,024 MAC/cycle, which would take 16 BOS INT8 8x8 arrays: 16 x 15,797 = 252,758 um2, i.e. +48.4% of the 4x4 composite. This mode adds +101 um2 inside the composite (+9,438 all-in, 1.81%).
- W4A8 at equal throughput needs 32 BOS INT8 (+96.9%).
- INT4 needs 64 BOS INT4 = 657,688 um2 (+126%).

**Peak area efficiency, 4x4, all-in:**

| precision | INT mode | dedicated BOS | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| INT8 | 770.9 | 1,620.5 | 0.48x |
| W4A8 | 1,541.8 | 1,620.5 (BOS INT8) | 0.95x |
| INT4 | 3,083.6 | 2,491.2 (BOS INT4) | 1.24x |

So INT mode is a reuse feature on INT8 and roughly competitive on low precision.

**Mixed SC+INT workload, INT fraction f = 5/10/30%:**
- Sequential (dependent) layers: INT mode gives 768 / 765 / 754 GMAC/s/mm2. The best-sized BOS add-on gives 614 / 575 / 529. INT mode wins.
- Only with perfect overlap does a BOS add-on win (806 / 828 / 929). That needs independent work concurrently on both engines, a separate memory path, and a BOS sized at f/(1-f) of the grid.

**Red-team verdict:** keep the INT mode as the default. A small BOS is only better for a throughput server with concurrent independent streams, and it should be judged on that system, not on GMAC/s/mm2 alone.
designs.verdict_on_user_shift_down_idea:
The shift should not be in the tile, and it should not happen every cycle.

1. PaYN's accumulator stays put for the whole reduction. In a time-serial digit schedule, the low bits of an output are only final after the last term of every weight has arrived. Bits shifted out each cycle would have to be stored and added back, which means a 24-26-bit rotating ring per tile (the lead's point (iii)).
2. A right shift, or the Horner left shift acc <- 2*acc + d, fights the segmented accumulator:
   - The pending carry/borrow must be flushed first.
   - All 24 state flops need a third D input. That is about +9.4 um2/tile with a 3-way mux, about 1.8% of a 4x4 grid; a 24-bit MXT2 row is 18.8 um2/tile, 3.7%.
   - 2*acc_low + 128 = 1150 overflows the 11-bit low_sum range of [-128, 1023].
3. It buys no throughput. Putting the weights in space already reaches the slot ceiling of 1 MAC/cycle/tile for one-product-per-lane INT8, with no shift at all.

The useful part of the idea belongs at the grid edge. The drain is already a serial stream ordered by digit weight (the east-most column holds the most significant digit), so the shift becomes one Horner register per output group in the east combiner, out = (H<<4) + s. That costs about 0.57k um2 per PE row, outside the composite. An LSB-first "shift down" combiner would also work there if the drain order were reversed, but MSB-first matches the existing chain at no cost.
risks: Drain-bound at short reductions. With 8 outputs per PE and an 8*P_C drain, INT8 utilization at L=128 is 0.30 (4x4) and 0.18 (4x8), and at L=1024 it is 0.77 and 0.63. Attention QK^T (L = head_dim 64-128) runs at under 30%. Per-PE drain taps would cut the drain to 8 cycles, for about 75 um2/PE of acc_in gating (1.2k = 0.23% on 4x4, paid in SC too) plus 192 output wires per PE.
Operand bandwidth is 2.67x SC (1,536 vs 576 b/cycle on 4x4). If the memory system is sized for SC, INT8 runs at no more than 0.375 MAC/cycle/tile. Bit-plane turbo needs 4 b/MAC (8,192 b/cycle).
Batch-1 GEMV: only 2 activation rows per PE, so 12.5% utilization on 4x4 at batch 1. That is better than SC (3%) but still poor; it needs batch >= 2*P_R.

Edge E2 depends on the compile-time scramble masks being the same on every edge, as they are today. If SCRAMBLE strides or salts change, the preset and per-lane code tables must be regenerated with --search (seconds). No lane-independent code table was found, so the feeder needs 8 per-lane tables per side.

Feeder and combiner areas (radix-16 code table 8.6-11.9 um2/lane, 576-bit port mux, about 0.57k combiner per PE row) are hand estimates. Synthesis is needed. The grid composite also excludes grid wiring.
The Sobol preset is not in RTL yet: sobol_bank needs a per-lane preset parameter and an INT strobe; returning to SC relies on the async reset.
INT-mode power is not characterized: per-cycle reload of 1,152 peripheral flops per edge half, sign pipes, and the -16N row toggling every cycle.

Bit-plane turbo (2/4/8 MAC/cycle/tile, zero tile change) needs edge E1. That puts 3.2k um2 in a 4x4 composite (0.62%) and one OR2 on the +0.307 ns comparator path, and it only beats Booth for L above ~4.3k (4x4) or ~9k (4x8). It is not recommended unless long-K INT layers dominate and memory supplies about 4 b/MAC.

The evidence is a Python model faithful to the RTL, not RTL or gate-level simulation. The cycle counts assume the grid's global mac_en/shift_in and that next-tile injection overlaps the drain, as modelled.
